summary.runtime_layer_recommendation: Compress these findings into a small English rule layer in PROD-053B after review.
summary.research_scope: English sales-call psychology, with general human psychology only where it directly improves sales-call naturalness or safety.

source_registry.title: Franke and Park adaptive selling/customer orientation meta-analysis
source_registry.usefulness: Adaptive selling improves performance only when the seller can recognize the situation and alter the approach.

source_registry.title: Adaptive selling integrative framework
source_registry.usefulness: A useful agent needs situation categories plus a small strategy library, not one universal script.

source_registry.title: Salesperson listening meta-analysis
source_registry.usefulness: Listening supports trust, satisfaction, loyalty, adaptive selling, and relationship outcomes.

source_registry.title: Perceived listening work-outcomes meta-analysis
source_registry.usefulness: Listening is most strongly tied to relationship outcomes such as trust and satisfaction.

source_registry.title: Gartner Challenger Sales Model overview
source_registry.usefulness: Useful selling can teach one relevant reframe before pitching, but only if claims are campaign-supported.

source_registry.title: Gartner modern B2B buyers and information overload
source_registry.usefulness: Buyers often struggle to buy because of complexity, information overload, and internal change risk.

source_registry.title: HBR customer indecision and no-decision sales losses
source_registry.usefulness: No decision is often a risk/confidence problem, so the agent should lower perceived risk without pressuring.

source_registry.title: Bain B2B Elements of Value
source_registry.usefulness: B2B buyers still have personal concerns such as reputation, risk reduction, and anxiety reduction.

source_registry.title: Mayer, Davis, and Schoorman organizational trust model
source_registry.usefulness: Trust objections should be separated into ability, benevolence, and integrity gaps.

source_registry.title: NCBI Bookshelf motivational interviewing chapter
source_registry.usefulness: Open questions, affirmations, reflections, and summaries help show understanding without forcing agreement.

source_registry.title: Empathy in motivational interviewing and language synchrony
source_registry.usefulness: Simple reflection can repeat or rephrase, but empathy is broader than parroting customer words.

source_registry.title: Frontiers reactance and persuasive communication review
source_registry.usefulness: Controlling language can trigger resistance; preserve real choice when recommending next steps.

source_registry.title: Ryan and Deci self-determination theory
source_registry.usefulness: Autonomy, competence, and relatedness are useful filters for sales wording; pressure undermines autonomy.

source_registry.title: Leader autonomy support meta-analysis
source_registry.usefulness: Autonomy support uses perspective-taking, choice, and informational rather than controlling language.

source_registry.title: Stanford Fogg Behavior Model
source_registry.usefulness: When action does not happen, motivation, ability, or prompt may be missing; do not treat all hesitation as resistance.

source_registry.title: COM-B behaviour change wheel
source_registry.usefulness: Classify friction as capability, opportunity, or motivation before choosing a response.

source_registry.title: Oxford conversation analysis overview
source_registry.usefulness: Partial repeats and targeted question words can locate a specific trouble source in a prior turn.

source_registry.title: Repair as interface between interaction and cognition
source_registry.usefulness: Repair practices help resolve trouble in speaking, hearing, and understanding before continuing.

source_registry.title: Amazon Alexa design principle: Be brief
source_registry.usefulness: Spoken agents should be brief, active, simple, and low-friction to avoid cognitive load.

source_registry.title: Google conversation design quick reference
source_registry.usefulness: After asking a question, stop speaking and let the user answer.

source_registry.title: Digital.gov clear and short plain-language guide
source_registry.usefulness: Use short sentences and one idea per sentence.

source_registry.title: CDC plain language checklist
source_registry.usefulness: Plain language should be understandable the first time people hear it.

source_registry.title: NIH plain language guide
source_registry.usefulness: Remove padding, stay direct, and keep one idea per sentence.

source_registry.title: Samuelson and Zeckhauser status quo bias
source_registry.usefulness: Doing nothing is a powerful default; make review steps feel reversible and low-risk.

source_registry.title: Iyengar and Lepper choice overload
source_registry.usefulness: Too many options can reduce action; offer one or two next-step paths, not a menu.

source_registry.title: Harvard Program on Negotiation BATNA explainer
source_registry.usefulness: A good sales next step should leave the buyer's no-deal alternative visible instead of hiding it.

topic_findings.finding: Useful adaptation needs situation recognition, confidence to alter the approach, a strategy library, and feedback from the interaction.
topic_findings.agent_use: Classify the customer move first, then pick one small response pattern. Do not use one universal objection script.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not infer personality or hidden emotion to choose a strategy.

topic_findings.finding: Listening and reflective responses are trust-building behaviors, but reflection is not the same as repeating everything the customer said.
topic_findings.agent_use: Use a short acknowledgement or one targeted reflection before answering. Mirror only a short phrase when it helps repair or invites elaboration.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not echo full customer categories such as boss, manager, spouse, and partner in every response.

topic_findings.finding: Many stalled sales are not lost to a competitor; they stall because the buyer is overloaded, uncertain, or safer doing nothing.
topic_findings.agent_use: Reduce decision load and risk. Preserve relief language, but say it like a person: no commitment today; take a look and let me know.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not answer an uncertain buyer by adding more facts, more options, or a bigger commitment ask.

topic_findings.finding: People resist persuasive messages when they feel their freedom is being threatened or the next step is a hidden commitment.
topic_findings.agent_use: Use real choices and explicit permission. Keep the buyer's ability to pause, compare, decline, or ask for a human visible.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not use must, have to, obviously, last chance, or false-choice closes.

topic_findings.finding: A hesitation can come from missing motivation, ability/capability, opportunity/context, or timing.
topic_findings.agent_use: When the customer hesitates, lower friction or ask a tiny clarifier before proposing the next step.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not treat every hesitation as a closeable objection or pressure problem.

topic_findings.finding: Trust concerns are not all the same: the buyer may question competence, whether the offer is in their interest, or whether the claim is honest.
topic_findings.agent_use: Answer the trust gap that is actually present: proof for ability, low-pressure fit for benevolence, limits and verification for integrity.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not use testimonials, confidence, or reassurance as a universal trust answer.

topic_findings.finding: Conversation repair should identify a specific trouble source instead of restarting the whole pitch.
topic_findings.agent_use: Use short repair moves such as 'the setup part?' or 'what changed?' only when the customer meaning is unclear.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not ask broad discovery questions after the customer already gave enough detail.

topic_findings.finding: Live spoken agents should use short, active, simple turns with one idea per sentence and should stop after asking a question.
topic_findings.agent_use: Keep most English sales turns to one or two breaths: acknowledgement, answer, relief or next step, stop.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not stack policy explanations, product facts, social proof, and a question in one turn.

topic_findings.finding: Insight-led selling is useful when it helps the buyer understand the situation, not when it manufactures urgency or pain.
topic_findings.agent_use: Offer one campaign-supported reframe only after a direct factual answer or when the buyer asks why this matters.
topic_findings.avoid: Do not use fear, scarcity, invented benchmark claims, or emotional manipulation.

compact_candidate_rules.name: Listen, answer, then continue.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: Start with a tiny acknowledgement, answer the customer move, then offer one low-friction next step.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: Of course. I can send it over. No commitment today. Take a look and let me know.
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: I can send a summary for your manager or spouse and there is no decision or commitment required from you today.

compact_candidate_rules.name: Keep relief, remove policy tone.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: If a safety or pressure boundary matters, say the relief plainly and briefly instead of explaining the whole policy.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: No commitment today. Just take a look and let me know.
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: There is no decision, no payment, no commitment, and no binding agreement required from you on this call.

compact_candidate_rules.name: Mirror only when it does work.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: Use a short partial repeat only to show listening, repair ambiguity, or invite elaboration; otherwise do not repeat the customer's category.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: Your boss? Got it. What would they care about most, price or setup?
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: Of course, I can send a short summary for your boss so your boss can review it.

compact_candidate_rules.name: One small decision per turn.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: When the buyer is uncertain, ask for or offer only one small next step instead of asking them to process the whole sale.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: I can keep it simple and send the two main points first.
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: I can send the summary, explain pricing, compare options, book a call, and include the contract terms.

compact_candidate_rules.name: Diagnose friction, not personality.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: Treat hesitation as possible relevance, ability, authority, risk, or timing friction; never label the buyer's personality or hidden emotion.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: Is the main thing price, timing, or who needs to review it?
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: It sounds like you are anxious about deciding.

compact_candidate_rules.name: Make autonomy visible.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: Use real options and make pause, review, decline, or human handoff acceptable outcomes.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: We can leave it there for today, or I can send the short version.
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: You should at least book the next call so you do not miss the opportunity.

compact_candidate_rules.name: Answer the specific trust gap.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: For trust concerns, identify whether the gap is ability, interest, or honesty, and answer only that gap.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: I do not want to overclaim that. I can send what is verified, and a specialist can cover the technical part.
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: You can trust us; many people are happy with it.

compact_candidate_rules.name: Ask, then stop.
compact_candidate_rules.rule: If the agent asks a question, it should not add another explanation after the question.
compact_candidate_rules.example_good: What would be most useful in the summary?
compact_candidate_rules.example_bad: What would be most useful in the summary? I can include pricing, terms, setup, and next steps if that helps.

rejected_or_deferred_tactics.name: False scarcity or fake urgency
rejected_or_deferred_tactics.reason: It can increase pressure and reactance, and it violates the project's low-pressure sales boundary.

rejected_or_deferred_tactics.name: Hidden emotion diagnosis
rejected_or_deferred_tactics.reason: Emotion signals are weak context; hidden-state certainty is already blocked by existing project policy.

rejected_or_deferred_tactics.name: Commitment traps
rejected_or_deferred_tactics.reason: Turning a soft yes into obligation conflicts with autonomy, trust, and no-commitment relief.

rejected_or_deferred_tactics.name: Full customer-category echoing
rejected_or_deferred_tactics.reason: Repeating boss, spouse, manager, or partner every time sounds scripted and does not add useful listening evidence.

rejected_or_deferred_tactics.name: Large live psychology planner
rejected_or_deferred_tactics.reason: A heavy reasoning layer can add latency. Research should be compressed into deterministic, reviewed rules first.

rejected_or_deferred_tactics.name: General persuasion principles without source mapping
rejected_or_deferred_tactics.reason: Generic tricks such as reciprocity, liking, and social proof are too easy to misuse unless tied to a safe, source-backed response rule.

notes: Research packet stores paraphrased project-owned findings only.
Compact rule candidates are not runtime-promoted in this checkpoint.
